name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 8
aliases: Combined Mitochondrial Respiratory Chain Deficiency Type 8

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Early onset multisystemic symptoms including neurological and muscular involvement
Deficient activities of multiple mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear genes affecting mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
Brain MRI showing basal ganglia and brainstem abnormalities
Elevated lactate levels in blood or cerebrospinal fluid

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early multisystemic clinical features plus biochemical evidence of combined respiratory chain deficiency and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

searchTerms: very high lactic acid in blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Combined deficiency of multiple mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes
pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by enzymatic assays in muscle biopsy

common.notes: Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones

occasional.notes: Enlarged liver due to mitochondrial dysfunction

searchTerms: endocrine issues including high blood sugar

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Reduced activities of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV in muscle biopsy
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia and brainstem signal abnormalities
Muscle MRI demonstrating fatty infiltration and atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components or assembly factors
Mitochondrial DNA depletion or multiple deletions may be present
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial morphology by electron microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant neurological symptoms with less multisystem involvement
Characteristic symmetrical lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem on MRI
Often associated with specific mitochondrial or nuclear gene mutations

redFlags: Rapidly progressive neurological deterioration in infancy
Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
Multisystem involvement including cardiomyopathy and liver dysfunction
references: Rahman S, et al. Mitochondrial disease: clinical features and diagnosis. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2017;40(4):569-580.
Parikh S, et al. Diagnosis and management of mitochondrial disease: a consensus statement from the Mitochondrial Medicine Society. Genet Med. 2015;17(9):689-701.
